title: Who’s in and who’s out? A case study of multimodal CLIP-filtering in DataComp
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the differential filtering rates (pass rates) of image-text data containing keywords associated with specific religious groups by the OpenAI CLIP model. It analyzed which religious groups are disproportionately excluded or included by the filter.
findings: The study found differential filtering pass rates for data associated with religious keywords. Specifically, data with keywords related to an 'Asian and Christian' intersection had relatively low pass rates, while data with 'European and Christian' keywords had relatively high pass rates through the CLIP filter. Keywords for 'muslims' and 'jews' were also analyzed, showing varying pass rates.
